maml:description.maml:para: Sends an email message using SMTP, SendGrid, or Microsoft Graph from within PowerShell. Replaces the deprecated Send-MailMessage.

The Send-EmailMessage cmdlet sends an email message using a variety of providers and authentication methods. It supports SMTP (with or without SSL/TLS), SendGrid API, and Microsoft Graph API. The cmdlet allows for rich email composition, including HTML and text bodies, attachments, delivery notifications, and advanced logging. It is designed as a modern, secure, and flexible replacement for Send-MailMessage.

Authentication can be provided via credentials, OAuth2, or provider-specific tokens. The cmdlet supports multiple parameter sets for compatibility with different authentication and provider scenarios.
Specifies the SMTP server to use for sending the email message. Required for SMTP scenarios.
Specifies the port to use on the SMTP server. The default is 587.
Specifies the sender's email address. Can be a string or a hashtable with Name and Email keys.
Specifies the reply-to address for the email. If not set, defaults to the From address.
Specifies the email addresses to which a carbon copy (CC) of the email message is sent.
Specifies the email addresses that receive a blind carbon copy (BCC) of the email message.
Specifies the recipient email addresses. Accepts a single address or an array of addresses.
Specifies the subject of the email message.
Specifies the priority of the email message. Acceptable values are Normal, High, and Low.
Possible values: High, Low, Normal
Specifies the encoding for the email message. Recommended to leave as default. Acceptable values: ASCII, BigEndianUnicode, Default, Unicode, UTF32, UTF7, UTF8.
Specifies the delivery notification options for the email message. Multiple options can be chosen.
Possible values: None, Delay, Never, OnFailure, OnSuccess
Specifies the delivery status notification type. Options are Full, HeadersOnly, Unspecified.
Possible values: Unspecified, Full, HeadersOnly
Specifies a user account or API key/token for authentication. Used for SMTP, SendGrid, and Graph API.
Specifies the username for SMTP authentication. Used with Password.
Specifies the password for SMTP authentication. Used with Username. Can be clear text or secure string.

Connects to an IMAP server and authenticates using credentials, OAuth2, or clear text.

The Connect-IMAP cmdlet establishes a connection to an IMAP server using MailKit. It supports multiple authentication methods, including OAuth2, PSCredential, and clear text username/password. The cmdlet returns an ImapConnectionInfo object containing connection details and the authenticated client for further use in subsequent cmdlets.

Supports advanced options such as certificate validation skipping, custom timeouts, and secure socket options. Designed for secure, flexible, and scriptable IMAP connectivity in PowerShell automation scenarios.

maml:description.maml:para: Connects to a POP3 server and authenticates using credentials, OAuth2, or clear text.

The Connect-POP3 cmdlet establishes a connection to a POP3 server using MailKit. It supports multiple authentication methods, including OAuth2, PSCredential, and clear text username/password. The cmdlet returns a PopConnectionInfo object containing connection details and the authenticated client for further use in subsequent cmdlets.

Supports advanced options such as certificate validation skipping, custom timeouts, and secure socket options. Designed for secure, flexible, and scriptable POP3 connectivity in PowerShell automation scenarios.
Specifies the POP3 server hostname or IP address to connect to.
Specifies the port to use for the POP3 connection. Default is 995 (POPS).

Specifies the password for clear text authentication. Required for the ClearText parameter set.
Specifies a PSCredential object for authentication. Used for OAuth2 or standard credential-based authentication.
Skips certificate revocation checks during the connection. Useful for environments with limited certificate infrastructure.
Skips certificate validation. Use with caution; only for trusted/test environments or self-signed certificates.
Specifies the secure socket options for the POP3 connection. Default is Auto. Options: None, Auto, SslOnConnect, StartTls, StartTlsWhenAvailable.
Possible values: None, Auto, SslOnConnect, StartTls, StartTlsWhenAvailable
Specifies the connection timeout in milliseconds. Default is 120000 (2 minutes).
